biggestGap: The pith ring is still a clipped near-white stroke — 69.6% of its pixels sit at R=255 on shots/r4/05-cut+500ms.png (round 3: 71.6%; reference lemon peel measured the same way: 0.02%) — so it still carries no shading gradient across its lit arc, and the directional ratio the round was supposed to raise to 1.8 went the WRONG way, 1.362 -> 1.164 against the reference's 2.11-2.41.

headline_probe_pith_ring_clipping_and_sw.method: REPRODUCED from r3-cutter.json's 'predecessor_classifier_probe': ring = pixels with min(RGB)>110, NOT peel (G>R+8), NOT flesh (R>G+35 & L>18), sat<0.45, outside the filled largest-flesh-blob mask and within a 7-iteration 3x3 dilation of it. Sector means over 12x30deg bins about the flesh centroid; clip fraction = pixels with R>=254.
headline_probe_pith_ring_clipping_and_sw.reproduction_check: On shots/r2/05-cut+500ms.png this method returns 71.1% clipped against the r3 critic's quoted 71%, and on shots/r3/05-cut+500ms.png 71.6% against their quoted 67%. headline_probe_pith_ring_clipping_and_sw.clip_fraction_R_ge_254: r2/05 71.1%  ->  r3/05 71.6%  ->  r4/05 69.6%.  r4/04-cut+250ms 60.4% (r3/04 61.2%). r4/08-citrus-caps 73.9%. REFERENCE 0.02%. The stated acceptance criterion was ZERO. Not met, not approached.
headline_probe_pith_ring_clipping_and_sw.directional_ratio: r3/05 1.362 (12/12 sectors) -> r4/05 1.164 (8/12 sectors, the dark spokes having dropped below the classifier's min(RGB)>110 floor entirely). r3/04 1.283 -> r4/04 1.157. Target was 1.8; reference 2.111-2.413. REGRESSED.
headline_probe_pith_ring_clipping_and_sw.r4_05_sector_luminances: 210, 209, 230, 219, 219, 198, -, -, -, 213, 230, - . The entire lit two thirds of the arc sits in a 198-230 band with 70% of its pixels pinned at R=255. That is a flat stroke, not a lit shell.
headline_probe_pith_ring_clipping_and_sw.ring_mean_rgb: r3/05 (243, 230, 189) -> r4/05 (241, 217, 171). The mean RED of the ring moved by 2 display levels in a round whose stated purpose was to give that channel headroom. Clipped subset means (255, 233, 189) with G at the 10/50/90 percentiles = 222/232/246, i.e. R alone is pinned while G and B are not: this is albedo x irradiance in the R channel exceeding the ceiling, not a white specular blowout, so the additive foam/specular terms are NOT the culprit and the arithmetic in the new albedo is simply wrong at the output.

unbiased_geometric_cross_check.why: The pale classifier is brightness-gated, so as the ring dims its own population changes and the clip RATIO is self-stabilising. A second, threshold-free probe: geometric band = distance 1..6px outside the filled flesh-face mask, inside the fruit silhouette (L>12, closed and filled), excluding peel (G>R+8). No brightness gate.
unbiased_geometric_cross_check.absolute_clipped_pixel_counts: 05-cut+500ms 850 -> 495 clipped px (29.4% -> 17.7% of a 2891/2790 px band). 04-cut+250ms 447 -> 242 (29.2% -> 19.7%). 08-citrus-caps 510 -> 280 (43.5% -> 22.1%). So the ring did get materially dimmer and about 42% of the clipped area went away — a real, measurable gain that the ratio probe hides. It is still an order of magnitude short of the reference's 0.02%.
unbiased_geometric_cross_check.band_sector_profile_r4_05: 96, 154, 147, 142, 153, 138 (lit) / 39, 43, 52, 35, 39, 40 (unlit), vs r3's 177, 178, 183, 179, 209, 211 / 87, 46, 36, 65, 70, 47. The lit arc dropped ~25-30% in luminance. The problem is that the top of that arc is still hard against 255 in R.
unbiased_geometric_cross_check.hue: Ring G/R 0.946 -> 0.901, B/R 0.780 -> 0.708, against plate-01's pith (168,137,95) = 0.816 / 0.566. Roughly a third of the hue gap closed; the band is warmer cream and less cold white than r3. Real but small.

evidence.blind_call: Instant, sub-second, same as round 3 and for the same reason. Crop the r4 lower melon half beside the plate-02 near lemon at matched size: the lemon's peel rolls continuously from a warm key at upper-left into unlit shadow at lower-right, never touching 255 anywhere, with a hard unlit edge against a defocused background. Ours is a cream annulus that sits at display 198-230 for two thirds of its arc with 70% of those pixels pinned at R=255, ringing a red disc dusted with white salt-speckle and hard black seed decals, inside a flat green rind that has visible blue patches at lower-left, all of it razor-sharp at every depth. The pith is still a stroke with a highlight drawn onto a disc rather than a lit shell.

fix: In src/fruit/species.js, stop trusting the simulated arithmetic and close the loop on the measurement. (1) The clipped ring pixels read (255, 233, 189) with G unpinned — R alone is over the ceiling, so pithC's RED component specifically is too high for the delivered irradiance: drop pithC (line 991) from vec3(0.5000, 0.4130, 0.2770) to approximately vec3(0.2900, 0.2400, 0.1610), holding the round-4 hue ratios, which targets a key-facing sector at display L~170 (the reference lemon's brightest peel sector) instead of the present 230. (2) Restore capKey's swing: species.js:303 currently returns amb 0.86 + gain 0.29 (peak/floor 1.34x); go to amb 0.34 + gain 0.92 (peak/floor 3.7x). The claim at species.js:129-136 that the layered-zone normal already supplies 3.6x of E-swing is falsified by the output — removing capKey's gain took the ring's directional ratio DOWN from 1.362 to 1.164. (3) Do not touch stage.js this round. Every round so far has moved an albedo and an exposure in opposite directions and netted zero; freeze the exposure and change only the albedo so the delta is attributable. Accept only when the reproduced ring probe reports clip fraction BELOW 5% (currently 69.6%, reference 0.02%) and a 12-sector ratio >= 1.8 (currently 1.164, reference 2.11-2.41), measured on shots/*/05-cut+500ms.png, 04-cut+250ms.png AND 08-citrus-caps.png.
